title: How does an app know which videos you might watch?
sources: Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations

lines.text: How does an app like YouTube or TikTok know exactly what video you want to watch before you even search for it?
lines.caps: How does an algorithm *read | your exact *mind?

lines.text: It doesn't just look at what videos you like; it tracks your behavior down to the millisecond.
Machine learning models measure watch time, how fast you scroll, rewatches, and where you pause.
lines.caps: Measures watch time, *scroll speed | and where you *pause

lines.text: It groups your viewing patterns with millions of similar users into high-dimensional mathematical clusters.
lines.caps: Groups your taste with *millions | of similar *viewers

lines.text: Candidate generation algorithms filter hundreds of thousands of candidate videos down to a top hundred.
lines.caps: Filters millions of *videos | down to the top *hundred

lines.text: A deep ranking neural network scores each video on the probability that you will finish and share it.
lines.caps: Scores videos on the *chance | you watch to the *end!

lines.text: The algorithm doesn't read your mind; it simply predicts your habits with superhuman precision.
